column1: # subsdk0 is NintendoSDK_movie (main imports from it)
# 60 fps (30 on the Switch): the game's config caps Unreal at 30 (FrameRateLimit=30 in DefaultGameUserSettings.ini, which sets t.MaxFPS, and nvn.SyncInterval=2 in SwitchEngine.ini, the present
# interval 2 it asks for); the host writes t.MaxFPS 60 and nvn.SyncInterval 1 into its console variables (hle_fpslock.c), so the game asks for present interval 1 itself. Unreal steps the game by
# the time that really passed. DM_FPS_TARGET=30 (Documents/env.txt on the iPhone) keeps the game's 30 and saves power
# a 3D game: D-pad, right stick (camera) and L3 / R3 on the iPhone's virtual gamepad
# Unreal Engine 4.18: nninitStartup takes one address region for the whole engine (16 GB by default), which a NumberLineAllocator (main+0x177c4d0) hands out;
# the rewriter's engine-wide gate on the store of its size (dm/tools/ue_region.py; hle_svc.c) gives it what the alias region has room for: 4.06 GB. Until 2026-10-31 the game's argument
# -SwitchVirtualAddressSpaceSize=4064 capped it (game_args), in MB up to 4095 (main+0x177c440: atoi, and a larger number is taken as bytes; 4224 gave a 4 KB region and a crash in the
# allocator's Compaction at boot). Two cuts on the SDK 7.3.2 build (dm/tools/sdk_patches.py) put it 64 MB into the alias region: the node area 62 MB instead of 1 GB, and regions of 4 MB
# and more 2 MB aligned, as SDK 20. Engage's 5 GB block: 256 MB in front + 4.375 GB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 128 MB heap region (the game sets no heap)
# The engine's global shaders (Engine/GlobalShaderCache-GLSL_SWITCH.bin), the engine's own materials and the game's. Unreal Engine 4.18 keeps every shader inline in the cooked packages,
# zlib-compressed, in paks whose blocks are LZ5-compressed; the NSP script decodes them on the Mac with the game's own LZ5 (uepak.py, shader_split.py ue_legacy_jobs, DM_OODLE_SERVE)
